earlyEstimate.note: NHTSA early estimates for 2025 (Crash Stats DOT HS 813 768 and 813 800) report a pedalcyclist percentage change, not a person-level file. GetCrashesByPerson requires an exact age, sex, seat, and injury, so it is not a census extract. No 2025 FARS rows were created from those estimates.

penndot.scope: Pennsylvania statewide, bicycle-involved crashes with a bicyclist death, suspected serious injury, or any injury
penndot.date: year and month only; occurredOn is the first of the month

news.note: The Nov. 19 sweep publishes the Nov. 18 Bay County death of an unnamed 58-year-old Marianna man on Panama City Beach Parkway at North Lakeshore Drive, the Nov. 18 Pell City life-threatening injury at US 231 and Comer Avenue, the Nov. 18 Sycamore e-bike injury at 1660 DeKalb Avenue, the Nov. 17 Goshen injury to Judah Peterson on Lakeview Drive, the Nov. 17 Farmington minor injury at Orchard Lake Road and Shiawassee Street, the Nov. 16 Pleasantville e-bike injury that named passenger Daniel Rodriguez Jr., the Nov. 16 Topeka minor e-bike injury at Southwest 29th Street and Wanamaker Road, the Nov. 3 Woodland Hills hit-and-run on De Soto Avenue, the Oct. 26 Long Beach hit-and-run on Pacific Coast Highway, and the Sept. 17 Kenwood death of Dallas Pickett, who died Oct. 5. The Alton row stays pending because police said the man was pushing a bicycle, not riding it. The Tyler row stays pending because police said no injuries were reported and also that the extent was unknown. The Apex headline is the existing Nov. 7 Holly Springs crash that killed Patrick Allen Turner. A Haddam e-bike crash and a Portland sleepover e-bike crash had no motor vehicle. The August Menifee death was an off-highway electric motorcycle and was already outside this window. The Oct. 28 Farmington death of Daniel Grechin-Pirogov was a person crossing on foot. The Nov. 18 sweep updates the Nov. 16 East Falls Church crash to a death after Arlington County police said the bicyclist died; his name was not released. It publishes the Nov. 17 Las Vegas minor injury at Cactus Avenue and Jones Boulevard, the Nov. 17 Kailua injury when a 13-year-old rode a bicycle into a school bus, the Nov. 16 Kaufman County death on State Highway 243, the Nov. 13 Lake Worth Beach death of Skye Tyler Frisby on a Cycrown e-bike, the Nov. 11 Grass Valley hit-and-run that killed an unnamed 80-year-old man at Brunswick Road and Burma Road, and the Nov. 10 Rio Grande death of Sheila S. Smith-McGraw on Route 47. The Saint Peter headline is the existing Kasota Township crash that hurt Shawn Mitchell Bagley. The Elk Grove Willard Parkway report is the existing Nov. 5 serious injury. A Jensen Beach e-bike crash on Nov. 15 was a 3,300-watt motorbike-style vehicle and was not added. A Kalamazoo train death and an August Menifee off-highway electric motorcycle death were outside this vehicle window. Headline extraction, plus article checks for the Oct. 25-31, 2026 Google News window, and Nov. 1, Nov. 2, Nov. 3, Nov. 4, Nov. 5, Nov. 6, Nov. 7, Nov. 8, Nov. 10, Nov. 11, Nov. 12, Nov. 13, Nov. 14, Nov. 15, Nov. 16, Nov. 17, and Nov. 18, 2026 desk sweeps. The Nov. 17 sweep publishes six injuries and no deaths: the Nov. 16 East Falls Church critical injury at Washington Boulevard and Langston Boulevard, the Nov. 16 Litchfield life-threatening injury at Route 118 and West Chestnut Hill Road, the Nov. 16 Hyannis e-bike head injury at South Street and Pine Avenue, the Nov. 15 Kasota Township injury to Shawn Mitchell Bagley on Highway 99, the Nov. 14 Farmingville injury on Horseblock Road, and the Nov. 13 Sterling Ranch hit-and-run that seriously hurt a child whose name was withheld. The Riverside Adams Street extrication stays pending because the fire report does not resolve bicycle versus pedestrian. Chico Nord Avenue and Commerce Telegraph Road were already on file. The Nov. 16 sweep publishes the Nov. 14 Chico death in the 900 block of Nord Avenue and the Nov. 15 Commerce injury on Telegraph Road at the Atlantic Boulevard ramp. The Coral Springs e-bike case stays pending because the crash date is not stated and the report describes an intentional assault. The Nov. 15 sweep publishes the Oct. 27 Mobile hit-and-run that killed John Ensor Jr. and the Nov. 8 New Brunswick crash that killed Gary Southerland. The Nov. 14 sweep covers reports from Nov. 12 through Nov. 14. The Germantown row is published as a fatal crash. Sources disagree on the device: police and NBC10 say electric dirt bike, 6abc says illegal electric motorcycle, and FOX 29 says e-bike. The North Adams row stays pending because the rider hit a parked car and no moving motor vehicle was involved. The Torrance crash at West 220th Street and Normandie Avenue was two vehicles and was not added. The Elk Grove row stays a serious injury because no newsroom confirmed a later death. The Orion Township row stays pending because no motor vehicle was involved; a later report named John Reilly. Pending rows stay out of desk totals until promote-news-crash.mjs.
